messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing intermittent 3-4x p95 spikes in the KV-cache + batching path. pattern is small batches -> warmup eviction -> a different matmul kernel gets picked and latency jumps. happens under sustained traffic but not in short local runs.
srini: can you paste the nsys command you used to capture the run?
maria: here's the basic capture I ran on the repro host (shortened):
```
nsys profile -o out/warmup_trace --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=10 --force-overwrite \
  --capture-range=nvtx:KVCACHE_WARMUP_START-KVCACHE_WARMUP_END \n```
(most of our traces in the repo use trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt these days)
devon: a couple things that smell: 1) 10s capture on a warmup window can bias sampling — if the kernel handover is transient you may miss the full tail, 2) capture-range NVTX brackets are great but you need the markers placed exactly around the hot loop, otherwise you trap only the tail.
maria: yeah i suspected sampling bias. the problematic handover appears right after the eviction NVTX marker — like within ~200ms.
srini: try a bracketed capture that includes ~5s pre-warmup and ~20s post-warmup. also record continuous OSRT and NVTX so the timeline shows the context switch between kernels. example:
```
nsys profile -o out/warmup_bracket --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=nvtx:PRE_WARMUP_MARKER-POST_WARMUP_MARKER \
  --duration=30 --sample=cpu --force-overwrite
```
add NVTX markers: `nvtxRangePush("PRE_WARMUP_MARKER")` / `nvtxRangePop()` in warmup driver.
jon: +1 to longer capture. Also check sample interval — default sampling might be too coarse for short-lived handovers. If nsys supports `--sampling-interval` set it lower (e.g., 1000us) to increase temporal resolution.
devon: another gotcha: kernel-selection heuristics can flip when batch size crosses a threshold that changes workspace or register pressure. If your eviction changes sequence length distribution, the runtime may pick a different GEMM kernel. That shows up as a narrow but tall spike on the kernel timeline and a pattern of many small kernels preceding a large one.
maria: i'm seeing exactly that — timeline shows a ~10ms microkernel then a 60ms main kernel after eviction, and that 60ms is the regression.
srini: when you upload the capture, include both the full bracketed trace and a short high-res capture around the exact 1s window where the handover occurs. the high-res one can be ~5s with tighter sampling so we can zoom in on kernel launch ordering.
perf-bot: upload complete — warmup_bracket.qdrep -> gs://redwood-perf/traces/warmup_bracket_2735001234.qdrep :thumbsup:
maria: link received, thanks perf-bot. i'll annotate NVTX markers and re-run with 30s bracket + 5s tight window.
jon: also consider toggling `KV cache eviction policy` (batch affinity / evict size) and rerun to see if the kernel choice flips deterministically. if so we can add a heuristic: pin kernel variant for X ms after eviction to avoid jitter.
devon: for triage checklist:
 - bracketed capture (5s pre, 20-30s post)
 - NVTX for PRE/POST and exact eviction boundary
 - capture trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt to get OSRT kernel switch markers
 - shorter high-res capture for the 200ms handover window with lower sampling interval
 - compare cuLaunch / kernel durations in timeline, look for different cuBLAS/CuDNN variants (symbol names)
 - try reproducing by forcing batch size boundary in a synthetic driver

maria: perfect. i'll run both captures tonight and drop qdrep + a short export of the kernel timeline CSV. if we confirm heuristic flip we can add a short-term mitigation in runtime (sticky kernel for 500ms after eviction) and an experiment to find the right timeout.
srini: great plan. ping here when uploads are done and i'll take the first pass on the timeline.
maria: will do. thanks all :heart:
